summary: Codex GPT-6 Luna at effort max ran battleship on skill-craft 1.16.1 for 19.3 h: 39 accepted visits, two Backchain loops (7 and 4 passes) and 41 Improve passes in 9 children (360.3 min, 31%).

It ended blocked at system-test on two person-only browser cases while all 4 harness checks passed in ShipLoop's worktree; product-acceptance, release and the report never ran. 13 commands were refused (4 run-path copy errors, 3 contracts over budget, 5 results or an opening in the wrong shape, 1 blocked result under S-14), and the main thread peaked at 97.5% of its 258,400-token window with 34 compactions.

Conclusions: the hours went to how much Luna writes in its loops, not to packet size (plan passes 2 to 7 changed only confirm clauses and a label), and the block was a missing open-item route, not a product defect.

Learnings: three engine fixes this run prompted are released but not yet seen live (budget text and prompt trim in 1.19.0, the system-test open item in 1.20.0); the harness misread the run four ways: two are fixed (stage minutes, Improve children), one is fixed for new runs (plugin on a resume), one is open (refusal lines).
Next: one Luna run at xhigh with one Backchain pass checks a03, a06, a12, a13 and a17 together; before it, record refusal causes (a21), release the shape fixes (a25) and publish the v2 export (a09).

basis.P1: Bent by o24: the host chose to run two Backchain loops (7 and 4 passes); every stage transition was the script's (39 visits in state.md history, the revise replanned through the script, o04).
basis.P2: Bent by o03: the host still writes the Backchain loop contract; Improve contracts over budget were refused at start (3 of 13 refusals) and all 9 Improve children have a receipt.
basis.P3: Broken by o27 and o32 (an off-protocol step-plan loop chosen before its packet was read); bent by o05, o28 and o43 (13 refused commands, and the run went on after each).
basis.P4: Holds: the run advanced only through callbacks (39 accepted visits, revision 57), and the resumed session ended its turn only after the accepted blocked result (cli stop end_turn).
basis.P5: Broken by o36 and o42 (a plugin verdict and an Improve time the record got wrong); bent by o21 and o40. o18 and o31 are fixed on this run's regraded record.
basis.P6: Broken by o06: Sonnet passed battleship in 19.1 min while Luna blocked after 19.3 h; bent by o23.
basis.B1: Bent by o11, o12, o19, o29 and o30: plan passes 2 to 7 (92 min) changed only confirm clauses and a label; the owner chose one pass (a17).
basis.B2: Broken by o13 and o26: no script checked either graph in this run, and the accepted step-plan candidate fails invariant 4; bent by o25.
basis.B3: Broken by o14: a 20-step plan graph with no parallel groups mapped to one work item, and no later packet names it (fast-planning investigation).
basis.B4: Bent by o15, o20 and o22: half of each graph restates the acceptance criteria, and Improve reviewed each plan again after Backchain.
basis.B5: Examined, not rated: one revise during build (o16, SYS-PORT-09); whether the spec or sources showed it is unknown.

o01.title: Model-built Backchain contract overflowed the loop's state
o01.expected: A script writes every loop contract, sized to leave room for reports.
o01.observed: The model built it at about 16 KB. Its first report was rejected twice and the plan stage could not close.

o02.title: Improve openings of 12 to 16 KB
o02.expected: An opening leaves room for the first review report.
o02.observed: Luna wrote contracts of 11.9, 12.1 and 15.7 KB against a 16 KiB state limit. Fixed with a 9,216-byte budget refused at start.

o03.title: Step-plan Backchain contract of 11.9 KB, one rejected report
o03.expected: Every Backchain loop carries the size budget.
o03.observed: Only the plan stage had the budget text. The step-plan loop's first report was rejected once and the loop closed with 677 bytes spare. The fix is committed locally, not released. [Superseded 2026-10-04: 112b239c was released in 1.19.0 (19fa890d); no 1.16.2 release was made.]
o03.advice: The budget text at every Backchain stage shipped in 1.19.0 (a06) and has not met a looped run since: read the next Luna run's Backchain contracts first. Inferred: with the loop text printed only at plan since 1.19.0 (a12) and one pass by default (a17) the host writes this contract less often, but still writes it; only a script-written contract (a02) removes the guess.

o04.title: Implement returned revise and the item was replanned once
o04.expected: A plan flaw found while building goes back through the script.
o04.observed: The script accepted the revise outcome, issued a new step plan, and the chain resumed. Designed behaviour.

o05.title: The model drops a space inside long callback paths
o05.expected: The model runs the printed command exactly.
o05.observed: Three refused calls, each recovered in one turn. The run path is over 100 characters. After the o33 count's cutoff the run made a fourth run-path error, a run directory typed as '.../20261003/20261003-bad' (events.jsonl line 7203), also repaired by the next call.
o05.evidence: test/shiploop_e2e/evidence/codex-gpt-6-luna-1.16.1-battleship-20261003.json runs.luna1.failures (4 of 13 are run-path errors); /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/v1161-battleship-luna/events.jsonl lines 7203 to 7206 (the fourth, repaired by the next call); docs/experiments/shiploop-callback-failures-20261004/failures.json. Was 'luna1 status: ShipLoop failures 9', written before the regrade (13).
o05.advice: Keep the engine change deferred, as o33 decided: neither reopening trigger has fired (no 'unrecognized arguments' or 'no ShipLoop run directory' line in the five run directories of 2026-10-04, and every path error here was repaired by the next call). Check R1 and R2 again after the next long run.

o06.title: Sonnet passes what Luna fails
o06.expected: The fast gate predicts the slow, deep run.
o06.observed: Sonnet's plan stage took about 0.6 minutes (accept timestamps) and it never starts a Backchain loop, so the state overflow only appeared on Luna, hours in. Context differs as much: Luna's main thread peaked at 251,867 of its 258,400-token window (97.5%, a Codex peak includes the call's own output) with 34 compactions; the largest of the four Sonnet hello peaks is 271,220 of 1,000,000 (27.1%).
o06.evidence: /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/batch-sonnet/battleship (timeline.json: plan accepted 0.6 min after the previous accept); test/shiploop_e2e/evidence/codex-gpt-6-luna-1.16.1-battleship-20261003.json (plan 196.4 min; contextPeak 251,867 of contextWindow 258,400; compactions 34) and the hello exports beside it (contextPeak, contextWindow).
o06.advice: Treat the Sonnet gate as a check of the flow, not of depth, and keep one Luna run per release as the depth check. Inferred: a Sonnet case cannot reach Luna's path while the loop is the model's choice (o24), and a 1,000,000-token window never meets the compaction pressure Luna ran under, so a07 helps only once a loop is required.

o07.title: Repeat review passes are not the cost
o07.expected: Fewer review passes would make Luna much faster.
o07.observed: They are about 16% of the time and later passes keep finding real issues. No prompt change; a metric records passes per child. [Superseded 2026-10-04: measured bind to receipt, Improve took 360.3 of 1,158.5 minutes (31%) over 41 passes (runs.luna1.improveMin of the v2 export), not about 16%.]

o08.title: The harness graded correct runs as failed
o08.expected: A grade reflects the engine, not the harness.
o08.observed: The resume prompt named a bare CLI, a finished run could not be graded, and a retention check matched only headings. All fixed with tests.

o09.title: The credential check refused a plain description
o09.observed: 'session token: opaque UUID' was refused twice. Descriptive values are now allowed; real secrets are still refused.

o10.title: Plan loop pass 1 changed most of the graph
o10.expected: Each pass finds a material gap in the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close.
o10.observed: Pass 1 (11 min) found three gaps: F-1 a wrong supplier direction between the page and the server, F-2 an unindexed API concurrency obligation, F-3 an omitted browser recovery requirement. It edited 14 of 20 steps: +5.8 KB, inputs 56 to 58 (one new supplier edge, one new null-origin fact). The pre-loop candidate was recovered byte-exact (digest 9e321e3d) from pass 1's audit input; the script kept no copy.

o11.title: Pass 5 found a gap in Backchain's own metadata and changed no plan bytes
o11.expected: A pass that reopens the loop is about the product plan.
o11.observed: F-7 was a stale source label (SRC-8 authority) in Backchain's scratch metadata. The candidate digest was the same before and after (3853b978). The clean streak was already 0, so F-7 cost one extra confirming pass (pass 7, 4 to 12 min) plus its repair inside pass 5, not the whole 17 minutes. Correction of an earlier entry that said it reset the streak. No product impact seen.
o11.advice: Take the one-pass default (a17): under it pass 5 would not have run. The gap cost one extra confirming pass and no product change.

o12.title: Two clean passes close every loop and cost 26 minutes across the two loops
o12.expected: The closing passes are cheap next to what the earlier passes found.
o12.observed: Plan passes 6 and 7 (12 and 4 min) and step-plan passes 3 and 4 (6 and 4 min) changed nothing, as the stop rule requires. Plan pass 7 exists only because F-7 kept pass 5 from being clean. It is unknown whether any clean pass ever prevented a defect.
o12.evidence: test/shiploop_e2e/evidence/codex-gpt-6-luna-1.16.1-battleship-20261003.json backchain luna1-plan (passes 6 and 7: 12 and 4 min) and luna1-step-plan (passes 3 and 4: 6 and 4 min); each loop's scratch/backchain-*/until-loop-receipt.json: trivial streak 2 of 2.
o12.advice: Take the one-pass default the owner chose (a17) and reword B1 with it (a18). The 26 clean-pass minutes are the visible cost; the larger one is plan passes 2 to 5 (76 min), which changed only confirm clauses and a label (o19).

o13.title: The graph's structure is asserted by the model, not verified by a script
o13.expected: A ShipLoop script checks ids, references, cycles and sinks and writes a receipt.
o13.observed: The plan result says its structural status is unknown because no deterministic validation receipt exists. A duplicate step id (S20) was caught only by the model's own check before freezing.
o13.advice: The check exists now (a03: record-only, 1.19.0): confirm on the next looped run that every Backchain stage leaves a receipt. On this run's candidates (LEARNINGS 'Backchain graph check, I1 and I2') it passes every plan candidate once packaged, so it would not have changed the plan loop, and fails both step-plan candidates on invariant 4 (o26).

o14.title: A 20-step graph was mapped to one work item with no parallel groups
o14.expected: ShipLoop uses the graph's order, groups and sinks to run the work.
o14.observed: The plan graph has 20 steps and an empty parallel_groups list, and maps to a single item (W1). The step-plan stage then built a second 20-step graph for W1.
o14.advice: Decide what the plan graph is for (a05) before building on it. The fast-planning investigation found that no later packet names scratch/backchain-plan and that Improve reviews plan.md, so nothing consumes the graph; using it (B3 as written) or not asking for it at plan are the two sides.

o15.title: Both loops carry the same ten per-criterion verification steps
o15.expected: A fact already in the spec, the acceptance criteria, is supplied by the script, not planned again.
o15.observed: Plan steps S11 to S20 and step-plan steps S8 to S17 are one 'independently confirmed' step per criterion: half of the plan graph and half of the step-plan graph. Elaboration doubled the 10-step draft to 20 (20 minutes before the first pass).
o15.advice: Settle a05 first; if the plan graph stays, generate the per-criterion steps from the spec (a04) so the model plans only the build steps. Checked in the two candidate-plan.json files: plan S11 to S20 and step-plan S8 to S17 are one step per acceptance criterion.

o16.title: The item plan was revised during build for a port check
o16.expected: A closed plan is revised only for what could not be seen at planning time.
o16.observed: The W1 plan and test strategy were revised so SYS-PORT-09 checks the sanitized child PORT separately from its readiness probe port, after two loops and eleven reviewed passes. One instance; unknown whether the spec or sources already showed it.

o17.title: No comparison exists between a run with Backchain loops and one without
o17.expected: We know what the loops add.
o17.observed: Sonnet never starts a loop and runs four cases end to end in 8 to 40 minutes; Luna spends about 4.4 hours in two loops (263 min). The models differ, so neither run says what a loop would have found on the other.
o17.evidence: /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/batch-sonnet (four cases, no scratch/backchain-* directory); /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/v1161-battleship-luna scratch/backchain-plan and scratch/backchain-step-plan.
o17.advice: Wait: the next Luna run with one pass (a17) compares one pass with this run's seven on the same case at no extra cost; buy the comparison (a01) only if that leaves the loop policy open. No effect is set: whether to buy it is the owner's choice, not a miss of B1.

o18.title: Harness stage minutes move time between stages
o18.expected: Per-stage minutes come from the script's own timestamps.
o18.observed: By accept timestamps test-strategy took 94 min and plan 196 min; the harness reports 224 and 39. The totals agree within 5 minutes (385 and 380 through plan), so only the attribution is wrong.
o18.evidence: status_1003.py output against run/timeline.json; fixed by 3c604304 (A2, merged 9db0be37): the regraded result.json gives plan 11,782 s and test-strategy 5,658 s, equal to the accept deltas

o19.title: After pass 1 the plan loop only refined confirm clauses
o19.expected: Each pass either changes the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close.
o19.observed: Passes 2 to 4 (59 min) each changed one confirm clause (S2 inspect to execute, S4 inspects the dependency files, S11 made deterministic): +0.4 KB together, same ids, edges and produces. Passes 5 to 7 (33 min) changed nothing. Whether a stronger confirmation changes what gets built is the open question.
o19.evidence: review-records/action-2..4-review.json; candidate digests b66d62f0, b4567c04, bfd6b9f6, 3853b978
o19.advice: Take the one-pass default (a17). Inferred: one pass leaves the kind of confirm-clause defect passes 2 to 4 fixed; the plan's exit text makes the Outcomes rule pass 1's duty, which is the counterweight to watch on the next run.

o20.title: Step-plan passes 1 and 2 added steps for items the parent packet already required
o20.expected: A fact the packet already states is planned in the draft, not found by the loop.
o20.observed: Pass 1 (42 min) added rejection tests and docstrings the parent packet requires, and a style note (F-01, F-02). Pass 2 (55 min) added D3, covering README and local-skill fit and the entrypoint contract, and changed 16 existing steps, mostly inputs (F-03, F-04). Snapshots 6f971770 then 024b3dc3; passes 3 and 4 changed nothing.
o20.advice: Inferred: these passes belong to the off-protocol step-plan whole loop (o27, o32), whose text 1.19.0 prints only at plan (a12); if the next looped run starts no step-plan whole loop, close this with a12.

o21.title: The script kept no snapshot of the candidate at each pass
o21.expected: Every candidate a loop checked is recoverable from the run.
o21.observed: The frozen plan candidate (digest 9e321e3d in the freeze log) is no file in the run. It was recovered only because pass 1's audit input embedded a copy that hashes exactly to it. The step-plan loop kept review snapshots; the plan loop did not, and neither kept the bind-time step-plan candidate.
o21.advice: a03 also keeps a content-addressed snapshot of each checked candidate under run/backchain/<action>/ (1.19.0); confirm on the next looped run that the final candidate of each loop is among them.

o22.title: Each plan also gets a second whole-plan review from the mandatory Improve child
o22.expected: A plan is reviewed once by the loop that owns its convergence.
o22.observed: After Backchain closed, Improve reviewed the plan again: the plan stage took 44 min after the Backchain result (about 5 min of handoff, then 3 review passes; the last reports no new defect) and the step-plan stage 24 min. Whether Improve finds what Backchain would is untested.
o22.advice: Keep Improve's planning passes, as the owner decided (fast-planning D4), and compare them on the next Luna run (a24): this run took 4, 11, 3, 3 and 5 passes at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan and test-spec.

o23.title: Improve's plan reviews are one line each on Sonnet and 2.3 KB each on Luna
o23.expected: Behaviour does not depend on the model.
o23.observed: Sonnet's plan reviews run 98 to 439 bytes (battleship: 104 bytes each, 'No material finding, no edits'). Luna's are 2,352 and 2,319 bytes, each listing what was reopened and rechecked. An Improve-only arm is a weaker control on Sonnet than on Luna.
o23.advice: Record it as a difference between models, not an engine defect. Inferred: an Improve-only control arm says less on Sonnet than on Luna, so a comparison that leans on one (a01) belongs on Luna.

o24.title: Whether a plan gets a Backchain loop is the model's choice
o24.expected: The script decides what runs; the model never chooses the next stage.
o24.observed: The packet says the host 'may request' one Backchain action; nothing in ShipLoop requires or checks it. Luna ran two loops (263 min); all four Sonnet runs ran none: no Backchain scratch directory and no until-loop receipt, and the plan stage was accepted in 0.5 to 1.1 min.
o24.advice: Decide what the graph is for (a05); the decision also says whether the script requires, offers or drops the loop. Today the packet says the host may request one: Luna ran two loops (7 and 4 passes), Sonnet none.

o25.title: ShipLoop cannot tell from the plan result that a Backchain loop ran
o25.expected: The script can tell when a plan result claims Backchain evidence.
o25.observed: The 'Backchain standalone Until Loop binding:' marker the guidance asks the model to preserve is not in the plan result, its notes, its inbox copies or the step-plan result; it sits inside the cited until-loop-receipt.json. 28 of the plan result's 56 evidence refs point into a model-chosen scratch directory. Exactly one cited file in each result has the Backchain plan shape (the final candidate), but the run holds eight such files.
o25.advice: Have the export record the loop facts the run's own files hold (a23): the backchain_passes option and whether the last check receipt's candidate is the loop's final one, as the fast-planning plan handed to this work (I4).

o26.title: The reference validator rejects the accepted step-plan candidate
o26.expected: A plan the loop closes passes the structural check.
o26.observed: Pass 1's repair added discovered step D1 (the production Node entrypoint contract) with no consumer. lib.js invariant 4 rejects both step-plan snapshots (6f971770 and 024b3dc3). Passes 2 to 4 and Improve accepted it. The plan candidates pass once packaged; raw they fail invariant 6 because the stored groups are [].
o26.advice: The record-only check (a03) flags this candidate; nothing refuses it, by the I2 decision (a refusal after convergence forces a re-loop). Inferred: the step-plan whole loop that produced it was off-protocol, and its text prints only at plan since 1.19.0 (a12), so the case to watch is a step-plan repair.

o27.title: The step-plan loop ran an operation its packet does not allow
o27.expected: The model follows the packet; the packet allows the whole plan/draft operation only at the plan stage.
o27.observed: The step-plan caller packet names action plan, stage draft, workflow stage shiploop:step-plan, although step-plan may only request audit or revise (BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS has plan only). The 136-minute step-plan loop is off-protocol data, not a sample of the designed route. Superseded in part (2026-10-04): the packet text is not shown to be the cause, because the model chose the loop before reading it (o32).
o27.advice: Verify a12 on the next looped run: no step-plan caller packet asking for a whole plan/draft. If one starts anyway, look at carried context and SKILL.md (o32), not at more packet text.

o28.title: Backchain loop text and a six-file reading list are printed at every Backchain stage
o28.expected: A packet carries only what its step may do.
o28.observed: Since 1.16.0 (db61a4a7, a fix for stalled planning) the packets at spec, plan, step-plan, carry-forward and product-acceptance name six Backchain and Until Loop files (+86 KB, +40% required reading) and about 553 words of loop text, though only plan may start a whole loop. Luna opened Backchain SKILL.md ten times before the step-plan loop and read 29 whole reference files across plan and step-plan.
o28.evidence: git show db61a4a7; shiploop_prompts.py _backchain_guidance; shiploop_navigator.py resource list
o28.advice: Fixed in text by a12 (1.19.0: the list and loop text print only at plan, pinned by dry-run tests); mark it fixed once the next looped run's packets show it.

o29.title: Where the planning time went: 592 min for the first work item
o29.expected: Planning time goes to work that changes the plan.
o29.observed: Step-plan loop 136 min (23%, off-protocol), plan loop 128 (22%), Improve review loops 186 (31%), Improve opening files 35 (6%), producer stage work 107 (18%). Sonnet got the same packets and planned in 4 minutes, so packet size is not the driver; model effort and the loops are. The shares are inferred from timestamps.
o29.advice: The owner's two levers cover most of it: one Backchain pass (a17; plan passes 2 to 7 took 92 min here) and effort xhigh instead of max for Codex runs (04ad68a2, branch fastplan-1f1dd3). Improve, 31% of the run (o42), is the largest block left (a24).

o30.title: Per-pass rules contradict the lens index and the printed head
o30.expected: One rule per behaviour: screen the lenses once, read references by section.
o30.observed: convergence.md asks every pass for actual reads of the applicable cards and an all-42-lens screen, while technical-lenses.md says to screen all categories once and not paste the library into every call. Each review record is 36 to 39 KB, about 60% a copied lens screen. The printed head says never read a whole reference file; convergence.md says read the card and adapter reference in full.
o30.advice: No option yet: I2c in docs/shiploop-backchain-validator-comparison-plan-2026-10-04.md (planned) decides how the lens screen is printed and cited. Inferred: with one pass by default (a17) a loop screens once, so the repeated screens mostly go; the contradiction between the two references stays until I2c.

o31.title: The harness counts each Improve child twice
o31.expected: Run metrics count what happened once.
o31.observed: metrics.json improve_children counts each child's directory and its -bind.md file: 16 for 8 children, and 14 for the 7 children of this run. The exporter counts directories. The harness's stage minutes and per-stage turns misattribute time the same way; accept deltas are the fix.
o31.evidence: run/improve/*, metrics.json improve_children; export facts.md; fixed by 7eb7ee88 (R5): the regraded result.json reads improve_children 9

o32.title: The step-plan loop choice predates the step-plan packet text
o32.expected: A decision to start a loop comes from the packet the script printed for that stage.
o32.observed: The step-plan head the model received never mentions Backchain, and its next message says it is using the Backchain planning skill, before it opens the full packet. The whole plan/draft choice came from carried context (the plan-stage loop, and SKILL.md's stage-less wording), so trimming step-plan packet text can be neither credited nor blamed. One run, one model.
o32.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna events.jsonl: the complete output after select-work (a 5,250 B step-plan head with no mention of Backchain), then the model's next message; docs/shiploop-i2b-trim-planning-prompts-plan-2026-10-04.md
o32.advice: Read the next looped run for a step-plan whole loop before changing any text (a12). If it recurs, the levers are the carried context and SKILL.md's stage-less wording, or a script-written contract (a02), not the packet.

o33.title: Callback path typos cluster in one resumed Luna session; engine change deferred
o33.expected: The model copies the printed callback exactly.
o33.observed: 41 failed ShipLoop or Until Loop commands in nine runs. All six inserted-space paths sit in session 2 of one resumed Luna run (3 of 52 callbacks; session 1 had 0 of 41 under the same run name), so the run-name explanation is contradicted and session age is the leading, unproven cause. Every error was repaired by the next call (one by +2), 110 s in 18.8 h, no state change. Engine change deferred; reopen when a path typo appears in any other run (R1) or one is not repaired by the next call (R2).
o33.evidence: docs/experiments/shiploop-callback-failures-20261004/ (script and failures.json, reproduced byte-identical); LEARNINGS section on callback path typos

o34.title: Claude failure counts are lower bounds: the harness cannot see them
o34.expected: Run metrics count the failures of every host.
o34.observed: metrics.collect reads only ACP tool_call_update events, so shiploop_failures is empty for all seven Claude runs while the same runs hold 15 failing ShipLoop or Until Loop commands and 28 to 40 refusals behind exit 0. Claude failure counts are lower bounds, and earlier journal cells reading 0 for Claude are unmeasured. Fix is a metrics item (M1) that waits for the other session's metrics.py change.
o34.evidence: metrics.json shiploop_failures for the seven Claude runs; failures.json

o35.title: The Luna run ended blocked at system-test on two human-only browser cases
o35.expected: A step that needs something only a person can supply is recorded as an open item and the run continues with everything that does not depend on it (S-14).
o35.observed: All five registered Node suites passed on the real candidate (16 of 16). The test strategy, written three stages earlier, had planned two required browser cases that need a person with DevTools; system-test marked itself blocked and ended on the awaiting route, after the callback refused the first blocked result with the S-14 rule and the model resubmitted blocked. Cause found by reading the packets: a stage advances only with done, and the closing paragraph of Stage readiness and completion says a required case already due and not run prevents completing the stage; the system-test duties have no open-item route (release-verify has one). The host ended its own turn after a 9.29 h resumed session: 39 accepted actions in 19.3 h; product-acceptance, release-plan, release-check and the report never ran. Sonnet's battleship runs recorded the same browser limit as an open item and passed. All 4 harness checks passed in ShipLoop's worktree (result.json worktree_checks); the project root holds no product because the run stopped before release.
o35.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna: run/state.md (status blocked, stage system-test, revision 57), the system-test packet, docs/shiploop/test-strategy.md#browser-procedure-and-open-observation, result.json
o35.advice: Confirm a13 on the next run with a person-only case: system-test accepts done with the case as an open item and the run reaches release. Add S-14 to the expectations (a19) so step 2 can show this miss. Inferred: plan step S10 already planned the human browser report, so the block was visible at planning; the deferred earlier lever is to plan person-only cases as open items from test-strategy.

o36.title: A resumed Codex run grades the plugin as failed
o36.expected: A grade means the engine, not the harness: resuming a run does not change whether the plugin loaded.
o36.observed: The resumed process graded plugin as failed with no plugin listed, while the first process of the same run graded it true. The resume path carries no evidence of the original install, so a resumed Codex run reads as a plugin failure. Cause not traced; the process that graded it ran the harness code from before the exporter and the regrade fix. [Superseded 2026-10-04: the cause is traced: the resume branch dropped the first launch's plugin record, fixed for new runs by 2528c470; this run's invocation.json predates the record, so its verdict cannot be regraded.]
o36.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna result.json (plugin loaded [], process pass) against the first process's baseline row (plugin true, process false)
o36.advice: Read this run's plugin verdict as unknown, not failed. The fix (a20) carries the first launch's plugin record into a resume or regrade; confirm it on the next Codex resume, which should print plugin PASS.

o37.title: The same hello request costs more with each release
o37.expected: A pass on the fast gate predicts a pass on a slower run, and the same trivial request costs about the same each release.
o37.observed: Sonnet hello passes every time, with no failure the harness can see (Claude's are not measured, o34), but its cost read $3.30, $4.39, $5.37 and $7.33 across 1.16.1, 1.18.0 and the two 1.19.0 runs: 84, 94, 113 and 149 model calls (unique assistant messages; the harness's turns, which count assistant events, read 143, 167, 194 and 254). a22.goal: Do: record that this run's run-path typos were each repaired by the next call, change no code, and reopen the engine change on a path typo in any other run (R1) or one not repaired by the next call (R2). a25.title: Print each outcome's shape in the head and name the correction in every refusal
a25.goal: Do: release the refusal and packet-shape changes: the packet head prints the exact shape of each outcome the stage allows, and each refused result or opening names the field or heading to fix, each correction tested through the same gate. Files and symbols: _outcome_shape_lines, _result_contract_lines, _result_shape_problem and _opening_sections in skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py (branch rrr-edc892). Test: python3 -B test/shiploop-callback-contract.test.py. Done when: the change is released and the next Luna run has no refusal for a missing outcome, summary or opening section.
a25.why: For: 5 of this run's 13 refusals were shapes the head did not print, and the refusal did not say what to change. Against: the head grows by about 1,100 characters where a stage allows blocked and one more outcome. Verdict: built and tested; release it before the next Luna run.
